Dynamic diagram (deployment view): Token-based API authorization.
Requirement: Authenticate users and authorize each API request.

A User [Person] signs in through a Web sign-in page [Container: Web app] with a username and password. Both the User and Web sign-in page are outside AWS Cloud. The page collects and submits the credentials to Amazon Cognito user pool over HTTPS; the page does not verify the password. Cognito verifies the password, authenticates the user and issues tokens. The ID token carries user attributes, for example cognito:username = alex; custom:tenantId = T-001; custom:type = Customer; cognito:groups = [Customers].

AWS Cloud [Deployment node] encloses Amazon Cognito user pool [Container: Amazon Cognito], Amazon Verified Permissions [Container: AWS managed service], Backend APIs [Container: REST API], and API enforcement [Software system boundary]. API enforcement encloses only Amazon API Gateway [Container: AWS managed service] and Lambda authorizer [Container: AWS Lambda]. API Gateway enforces the authorization result; Lambda authorizer verifies the token and queries policy; Amazon Verified Permissions makes policy decisions.

The Web sign-in page sends the token with each API request to Amazon API Gateway over HTTPS. API Gateway passes the token to the Lambda authorizer using a generic AWS invocation. The authorizer verifies the token and asks the Amazon Verified Permissions decision endpoint over HTTPS whether the request is allowed. If allowed, API Gateway forwards the request to Backend APIs over HTTPS. If authorization fails, API Gateway returns HTTP 403 with an authorization error message to the Web sign-in page over HTTPS.

Represent the main sequence as 1. Authenticate (returns tokens); 2. API request with token; 3. Pass token for authorization; 4. Query policy; 5. Forward allowed request. A separate bold 5' relationship represents the HTTP 403 failure response. Policy query is auxiliary and dashed; main calls are solid. Arrows point from caller to callee; return tokens are folded into the authentication label, rather than a second return arrow. User uses the Web sign-in page. Show the token example in a local comment near Step 1 and explain the notation in a legend. All calls remain inside shared enclosing domains and cross only required boundaries.

Title: "Dynamic diagram (deployment view): Token-based API authorization"

Requirement: "Authenticate users and authorize each API request."

Elements and boundaries:

- A User, typed "[Person]," is outside the AWS Cloud deployment node.
- A Web sign-in page, typed "[Container: Web app]," is also outside AWS Cloud.
- The enclosing "AWS Cloud [Deployment node]" contains Amazon Cognito user pool, Amazon Verified Permissions, Backend APIs, and the API enforcement boundary.
- "API enforcement [Software system boundary]" encloses Amazon API Gateway and Lambda authorizer only.
- Amazon Cognito user pool is typed "[Container: Amazon Cognito]" and has responsibility "Authenticates and issues tokens."
- Amazon API Gateway is typed "[Container: AWS managed service]" and has responsibility "Enforces the authorization result."
- Lambda authorizer is typed "[Container: AWS Lambda]" and has responsibility "Verifies token and queries policy."
- Amazon Verified Permissions is typed "[Container: AWS managed service]" and has responsibility "Makes policy decisions."
- Backend APIs is typed "[Container: REST API]."

Directed relationships:

- User → Web sign-in page: solid arrow labeled "Uses web app."
- Web sign-in page → Amazon Cognito user pool: solid arrow labeled "1. Authenticate [HTTPS]" with "returns tokens" on a second line. The visible arrowhead points toward Cognito; token return is expressed in the label rather than as a separate return arrow.
- Web sign-in page → Amazon API Gateway: solid arrow labeled "2. API request with token [HTTPS]." It enters AWS Cloud and then the API enforcement boundary.
- Amazon API Gateway → Lambda authorizer: solid arrow labeled "3. Pass token [AWS invocation]." Both endpoints are within API enforcement.
- Lambda authorizer → Amazon Verified Permissions: dashed arrow labeled "4. Query policy [HTTPS]." This auxiliary relationship crosses out of the API enforcement boundary while remaining inside AWS Cloud.
- Amazon API Gateway → Backend APIs: solid arrow labeled "5. Forward allowed request [HTTPS]." This crosses out of API enforcement while remaining inside AWS Cloud.
- Amazon API Gateway → Web sign-in page: solid arrow routed back out of API enforcement and AWS Cloud, labeled in bold "5'. Authorization failure: HTTP 403 [HTTPS]." Its arrowhead points into the Web sign-in page. This is the failure response alternative to forwarding an allowed request.

A yellow folded note inside AWS Cloud, outside API enforcement, reads:

"Step 1: example token claims
cognito:username = alex
custom:tenantId = T-001
custom:type = Customer
cognito:groups = [Customers]"

Legend and interpretation:

- Solid arrow: "Main call; caller to callee."
- Dashed arrow: "Auxiliary policy query."
- Bold label: "Failure response."
- Service tile / actor: "AWS service / person."
- Plain white box: "Custom container."
- Outlined group: "Deployment node or system boundary."
- Folded note: "Local comment, not a service or boundary."

AWS services are represented with service tiles, the user with a person symbol, and the web app and backend with plain white boxes. No separate policy-decision return arrow or token-verification mechanism is explicitly shown. All text above was readable; no additional behavior is inferred.

The diagram is titled "Dynamic diagram (deployment view): Token-based API authorization." Its requirement is: "Authenticate users and authorize each API request."

Elements and boundaries:

- User, typed as "[Person]," is outside the AWS Cloud boundary.
- Web sign-in page, typed as "[Container: Web app]," is also outside AWS Cloud.
- AWS Cloud is an enclosing "[Deployment node]." It contains Amazon Cognito user pool, the API enforcement boundary, Amazon Verified Permissions, and Backend APIs.
- API enforcement is an enclosing "[Software system boundary]" inside AWS Cloud. It contains Amazon API Gateway and Lambda authorizer.
- Amazon Cognito user pool is "[Container: Amazon Cognito]" with responsibility "Authenticates and issues tokens."
- Amazon API Gateway is "[Container: AWS managed service]" with responsibility "Enforces the authorization result."
- Lambda authorizer is "[Container: AWS Lambda]" with responsibility "Verifies token and queries policy."
- Amazon Verified Permissions is "[Container: AWS managed service]" with responsibility "Makes policy decisions." It is inside AWS Cloud but outside API enforcement.
- Backend APIs is "[Container: REST API]." It is inside AWS Cloud but outside API enforcement.

Directed relationships:

- User → Web sign-in page: "Uses web app." This is a solid arrow without a step number or stated protocol.
- Step 1, Web sign-in page → Amazon Cognito user pool: "1. Authenticate [HTTPS]" with a second line, "returns tokens." This is a solid arrow. There is no separate return arrow drawn.
- Step 2, Web sign-in page → Amazon API Gateway: "2. API request with token [HTTPS]." This is a solid arrow entering AWS Cloud and API enforcement.
- Step 3, Amazon API Gateway → Lambda authorizer: "3. Pass token [AWS invocation]." This is a solid arrow entirely inside API enforcement.
- Step 4, Lambda authorizer → Amazon Verified Permissions: "4. Query policy [HTTPS]." This is a dashed arrow crossing out of API enforcement while remaining inside AWS Cloud.
- Step 5, Amazon API Gateway → Backend APIs: "5. Forward allowed request [HTTPS]." This is a solid arrow crossing out of API enforcement while remaining inside AWS Cloud. The stated condition is that the request is allowed.
- Alternative step 5′, Amazon API Gateway → Web sign-in page: "5′. Authorization failure: HTTP 403 [HTTPS]." The label is bold, marking a failure response. Its solid routed arrow exits both API enforcement and AWS Cloud and ends at the web sign-in page.

A folded yellow note inside AWS Cloud, near Cognito and above the API enforcement boundary, contains:

"Step 1: example token claims
cognito:username = alex
custom:tenantId = T-001
custom:type = Customer
cognito:groups = [Customers]"

The legend specifies that a solid arrow is a main call from caller to callee; a dashed arrow is an auxiliary policy query; and a bold label is a failure response. Service tiles and the actor represent AWS services and a person. Plain white boxes represent custom containers. Outlined groups represent deployment nodes or system boundaries. A folded note is a local comment, not a service or boundary.

All text described above was readable. No policy-result return relationship or additional authorization conditions are explicitly drawn.
